text:
anya: Headed into the weekend with a weird one — long chat sessions on the mistral-1.x route -> qwen-compat path show steady KV page growth, even after clients idle. Not obvious eviction happening.
hiro: ugh. any perf logs or kernel-selection traces?
anya: pasted initial runtime debug dump below. Nothing loud, just page_alloc counters climbing.
```
kernel_selector: picked kernel v2 (mqa-optimized) for model mistral-1x length_profile=long
kv_cache.pages_allocated=12834
kv_cache.pages_in_use=12740
kv_cache.pages_free=94
kv_cache.page_frag_pct=21.3
kv_cache.alloc_seq_tail=0x7fffa12b
batching.window=32
batching.mean_latency_ms=6.2
```
anya: after ~30min chat session pages_allocated -> 21721, pages_free still tiny, fragmentation up to 29%.
matt: can you repro with a single worker/process? or is this across multiple tasks?
anya: single pod, single worker. can repro with a scripted chat that sends long prefixes + lots of short followups.
hiro: initial suspicion: rope-scaling interaction with MQA/GQA split. if kernel selector flips kernels mid-session due to sequence distribution changes, we might be allocating different slab sizes and not coalescing properly.
ops-elisabeth: is eviction policy LRU or residency-age based? we had a change last quarter to favor residency for QoS.
anya: residency-based with hysteresis (60s warm grace). long sessions keep touching old prefixes so they never become cold. but eviction still expected when free pages < threshold, which is not happening.
hiro: could be fragmentation where free fragments are below min-page-size for new allocations -> allocator keeps growing journal instead of evicting. need allocator trace.
benchmark-bot: flagged related perf regression #4321 (regressed after kernel-switch heuristics PR).
matt: share /proc/pagemap-style snapshot and runtime allocator map. also include kernel_selector debug with timestamps.
anya: attached mini repro steps in case folks want to run locally:
```
# repro script (bash)
for i in $(seq 1 600); do
  curl -s -X POST https://redwood-host/api/v1/generate -d '{"model":"mistral-1x","input":"'"$(python - <<PY
print('x'*1000)
PY
)"}'
  sleep 0.5
done
```
anya: note: using model variant that our router rewrites to qwen-compat with kernel-fallback enabled.
hiro: next actions: 1) gather allocator live map 2) enable kernel_selector verbose to log kernel switch timestamps 3) try forcing kernel pin (lock to mqa/gqa) to see if growth stops.
matt: i'll run the pinned-kernel experiment on a canary. will post results. assigned to @hiro for bisect and @matt for canary.
ops-elisabeth: if this flares in prod we'll need an emergency fallback to dedicated-route (no kernel switching) — keep me posted.
benchmark-bot: canary started on infra-045, run id c-775. baseline mem growth: +78MB/15min; pinned-kernel run: +8MB/15min (initial).
hiro: early signal means kernel-switching correlates strongly. next try: reproduce with different quantization profiles (q8_0 vs q4f32) to see allocator stride differences.
anya: also observed slight change in batching heuristics when kernel flips: batching.window shrinks from 32 -> 8 intermittently. that increases churn and small allocations.
matt: interesting — the batching change could create many small KV writes leading to fragmentation. if allocator has minimum fragment size mismatch with kernel page layout we get stranded fragments.
hiro: plan: run localized bisect around PR that changed kernel selector thresholds + PR that adjusted batching autoshrink. i'll post PR links when I have the bisect range.
anya: created issue #5234 with logs and repro. dropping the quick debug commands here:
```
# runtime debug toggles
curl -X POST http://localhost:7777/_admin/debug -d '{"kv":"dump_map"}'
curl -X POST http://localhost:7777/_admin/debug -d '{"kernel_selector":"verbose_on"}'
```
anya: if anyone sees similar on other model families (llama/qwen variants) please ping here. this one feels like an allocator+kernel polyglot bug rather than model-only.
ops-elisabeth: noted. tagging on-call infra for monitoring: @matt and @hiro. I'll prep a short-run rollback playbook if canary fails. :clipboard:
hiro: will update in this thread after bisect. thanks for the repro, it helped a lot.
matt: canary results posted at 4753509755; looks promising but need longer run.
anya: thanks all. next update tomorrow with bisect results. :coffee:
